_comment: What to read out of Scaleway's public product catalog.
It names PRICING UNITS, not models. Which models Scaleway offers is Scaleway's
business and changes week to week; following that is the whole point of this job.
A model it adds is published on the next run, one it withdraws keeps its last
observed prices and gains an 'absent_since' stamp, and both show up as + / ~ lines
in the run summary and the commit.
There is no hand-written model list, and there must not be one. Each catalogue
entry states the callable model id itself, in 'product', so nothing needs
translating by hand -- not even from the sku, which spells the same id with
underscores ('/ai/generative_apis/consumption/qwen3_8_27b_input/fr-par').
The source is the public catalogue API behind scaleway.com/en/pricing/, not the
pricing page itself. Both carry the same figures (checked by hand on 2026-11-03,
all 17 models then on the page), but the page answers a plain fetch with a
Bunny Shield challenge -- HTTP 403 unless the request carries browser headers --
while this endpoint answers a keyless GET with JSON. The page remains worth a
look when a figure here is surprising: it is what a human is shown.
One entry per (model, unit type, consumption mode, region), so a model is
assembled from several entries. 'fields' below says which
(unit, size, token type, consumption mode) this repository can publish and under
which field; an entry whose descriptor is not in that table is skipped and
reported rather than guessed at, because the unit is part of the field name in
pricing.json.
'per' is the unit the published field is quoted in, 'size' the one the catalogue
quotes: a figure is scaled by per/size. Token prices arrive per 1000 tokens and
are published per million; audio arrives per 60 seconds and is published per
minute. Doing that with Decimal rather than a float multiply keeps 1.8 as 1.8
BATCH RATES ARE PUBLISHED, under the '_batch' suffix of the same unit. Scaleway
sells every model twice: served immediately at the listed rate, or deferred and
discounted in batch. Both are read from the catalogue, neither is derived from
the other, and the suffix rather than a separate section is what keeps the unit
in the field name -- in_per_mtok_batch is per million input tokens, in batch.
Do not compute a batch rate by halving the realtime one. It is usually half --
31 of the 32 batch rates on 2026-11-03 -- but not always: glm-5.2's output token
is 5.50 in realtime and 2.70 in batch, where glm-5.3's is 5.50 and 2.75. Halving
would have published a figure Scaleway never wrote, in the one case where it
matters. The 'batch' entries are read like any other row, so a model that stops
being sold in batch simply loses the field on the next run.
Deliberately NOT published, though the catalogue states them:
* every region but the one named in 'region'. All prices were fr-par when this
was written, and this file holds one price per model, not one per region. A
region other than that one is reported once per run rather than published.
* 'tasks' (chat, code, vision, ocr, audio_transcription, embeddings) and
'provider_name'. Useful labels, but this file classifies by billing unit and
by nothing else: OVH states no task list, Hugging Face states none, and Eden
AI states its own, so a task field would be filled for one provider in five
and invite filtering on something that is mostly missing. Decided with Simon
'published_statuses' is what Scaleway is willing to sell. An entry carrying any
other status is left out, and the entry this file already publishes for it gains
an 'absent_since' stamp through the shared reconcile_inventory(): 'end_of_life'
and 'retired' both mean the catalogue no longer offers it, which is exactly what
that stamp says. 'end_of_new_features' is still sold -- glm-5.2 carries it and
appears on the pricing page -- so it stays published.
This block publishes EUR, which is what the catalogue states. No conversion is
performed anywhere in this repository.
_comment_format: A JSON endpoint: asked for as JSON, and judged against a floor that suits a body of pure data.
